_about: How far the grand campaign's chart reaches. 'far' false: Europe and the Americas with their cities, as the cities version plays them. 'far' true: the whole world, with the Pacific and the globe laid after them (step 13 and the globe's stage) and the countries that live there. One line, flipped by the rules builder when the far side ships; until then nothing of the far side is read, so no campaign and no war moves. A test of the far side turns it on for its own file alone (src/campaign/stage.ts).
_convoyBattle: The wolf pack and convoy battle (release 2; Brian's yes of 20 November 2026, ruling 241 of 22 November). Off: nothing of the convoy battle runs, no extra die is thrown, and every war is the war of release 1. On: the grand campaigns opened from now on carry the flag 'convoyBattle' (set at a campaign's start only, never in one under way): every month on a convoy route takes a swing (data/campaign/convoybattle.json), and a night the player fights is booked back through navy.ts convoyField. A run outside the browser can be given it by TC_CONVOY=1.
_fortRows: The fortress rows (the design director's 05:38Z-06:21Z of 22 November 2026; data/campaign/fortrows.json): the book's fortress crews by date, taking no place among the five, their works holding all round, and beaten crews staying in their works as the town's garrison on their own stores. Off, the game is release 1's, war for war. A run outside the browser can force it: TC_FORTS=1 or TC_FORTS=0.
_yieldRule: The yield form (the design director's 05:30Z, 06:41Z and 07:20Z of 22 November 2026; data/campaign/capitulations.json; src/campaign/yield.ts): a beaten country yields when its field army is beaten and no ally's relief can reach it, and at stops 1-2 a computer-run country yields in the record's month after the first blow. A second way in beside the fall that release 1 has. Off, the game is release 1's, war for war. A run outside the browser can force it: TC_YIELD=1 or TC_YIELD=0.
_bargains: A neutral's bargains (release 2; Brian's yes of 22 November 2026, the design director's frame of 03:42 UTC and ruling of 03:47 UTC). Off: nothing of src/campaign/bargains.ts runs and every war is the war of release 1. On: the grand campaigns opened from now on carry the flag 'bargains', and their neutrals sell their goods to whichever country at war bids best (data/campaign/bargains.json). A test turns it on for its own games by setting that flag; a run outside the browser by TC_BARGAINS=1.
_legions: Volunteer legions (release 2; Brian's yes of 22 November 2026, the design director's frame of 03:42 UTC and rulings of 03:47 and 03:55 UTC). Off: nothing of src/campaign/legions.ts runs and every war is the war of release 1. On: the grand campaigns opened from now on carry the flag 'legions', and a country at peace outside both sides may send one legion of volunteers at a time to fight in a patron's army (data/campaign/legions.json). A test turns it on for its own games by setting that flag; a run outside the browser by TC_LEGIONS=1.
_winChance: The honest win chance on land (release 2; auto-resolve fix 1, Brian's yes of 23 November 2026 07:11Z and the design director's orders of 07:06Z, 07:27Z and 10:14Z; data/campaign/winchance.json). Its own step inside Units decide: it needs 'unitsDecide' too, and stays off, card and field both, until the 3D field's win share by odds band is within a tenth of the card's curve. Off: every battle throws today's luck and nothing changes. On: the grand campaigns opened from now on with Units decide carry the flag 'winChance' as well, and an attack in the field carries the ground at the record's rate for its odds (wider luck, losses unchanged). A test turns it on for its own games by setting both flags; a run outside the browser by TC_UNITS=1 TC_WINCHANCE=1.
_unitsDecide: Units decide (release 2; Brian 23 November 2026 07:11Z and 07:13Z, the core theme; the design director's audit of 07:17Z): battles come from the units each side built, researched and trained, never from a nation's flag or the date (src/campaign/units.ts). Off: nothing behind it is read and every war is the war without it. On: the grand campaigns opened from now on carry the flag 'unitsDecide' (set at a campaign's start only). Its steps so far: the convoy war by cause (data/campaign/convoycause.json). A run outside the browser can force it: TC_UNITS=1 or TC_UNITS=0.
_nicknames: Earned nicknames (release 2; Brian's yes of 23 November 2026 12:05Z; src/campaign/nicknames.ts, data/campaign/nicknames.json): a corps that wins several hard fights is given a name by its own army, in its nation's own style, and the name is shown on its flag. Every nation alike; a name changes no number. Off: nothing of it is read and every war is the war without it. On: the grand campaigns opened from now on carry the flag 'nicknames' (the player can also turn it on or off in a campaign under way: a name is only a name). A run outside the browser can force it: TC_NICKNAMES=1 or TC_NICKNAMES=0.
_columns: Supply columns (release 2; Brian's yes of 23 November 2026 12:05Z; src/campaign/columns.ts, data/campaign/columns.json): every month lorry columns drive from each nation's railhead along the roads to its corps beyond it, and enemy aircraft or partisans can ambush them on the way; what is lost never reaches the front. Outcomes come from what is on the ground and in the air (escorts, air cover, the partisans' strength), never from a nation or a date. Off: nothing of it is read and every war is the war without it. On: the grand campaigns opened from now on carry the flag 'columns' (set at a campaign's start only). A run outside the browser can force it: TC_COLUMNS=1 or TC_COLUMNS=0.
_logistics: Three supply orders on top of the supply columns (release 2; Brian's yes of 23 November 2026 13:06Z; src/campaign/logistics.ts, data/campaign/logistics.json), each its own switch and each read only where the columns run: 'lorryShift' (a nation's lorries are as many as its industry and fuel give, and go first to the front it names), 'wagons' (horse-drawn wagons carry what the lorries cannot, slower, and the ground tells on both) and 'dumps' (forward dumps stocked beyond the railhead feed the corps near them by a shorter road; bombing burns them and losing the ground loses them). Off: nothing of them is read. On: the grand campaigns opened from now on carry the flag (set at a campaign's start only). Forced by TC_LORRYSHIFT, TC_WAGONS, TC_DUMPS (1 or 0).
_fleetAttack: A fleet sent straight at an enemy fleet (release 2; Brian 23 November 2026 22:23Z: drag a fleet onto theirs and the battle is fought, as an army attacks; src/campaign/fleetattack.ts, data/campaign/fleetattack.json). The player's own order, in his month, at any odds, told them first, at sea or in the enemy's harbour. Off: nothing of it is read, no die is thrown and every war is the war without it. On: the grand campaigns opened from now on carry the flag 'fleetAttack' (the player can also turn it on or off in a campaign under way). A run outside the browser can force it: TC_FLEETATTACK=1 or TC_FLEETATTACK=0.
_breakUp: Breaking a corps up (release 2; Brian 24 November 2026 18:02Z: "when I click on a unit stack, I want to be able to see each individual unit apart of it. that way i can break it up if needed"; src/campaign/breakup.ts, data/campaign/breakup.json). The player picks divisions of one of his corps and splits them off as a corps of their own where it stands; a part rejoins the corps it came from. Off: nothing of it is read and every war is the war without it. On: the grand campaigns opened from now on carry the flag 'breakUp' (the player can also turn it on or off in a campaign under way). A run outside the browser can force it: TC_BREAKUP=1 or TC_BREAKUP=0.
_marked: The marked army (release 2; Brian 24 November 2026 18:01Z, 'yes to all', the third idea of the enemy's month near you; src/campaign/marked.ts): the enemy corps that takes one of the player's towns wears a red tag on the table, and its card says what it took, until he beats it; beating it, or its end, clears the mark with a line of news. No more than three at once. A mark changes no number. Off: nothing of it is read and every war is the war without it. On: the grand campaigns opened from now on carry the flag 'marked' (the player can also turn it on or off in a campaign under way). A run outside the browser can force it: TC_MARKED=1 or TC_MARKED=0.
